newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 6.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** Former civil aviation minister Madhavrao Scindia, a key member of India's ruling United Front alliance, switches back to the Congress party
Move likely to trigger the return of more splinter
groups to the Congress party posing a threat to the minority ruling coalition which depends on Congress' support in parliament, Indian newspapers say
** Democrat Bill Clinton re-elected U.S. president for second term, blowing away Republican Bob Dole
** Former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao appeals to higher court against magistrate's order denying him bail in a forgery case. The court likely to take up plea on Wednesday
** Finance Minister P. Chidambaram forecasts GDP growth of about 6.5 in 1996/97 (April-March) against revised 6.6 percent in 1995/96
** India's 1996/97 foodgrain output seen up at 196.3 million tonnes versus 185 in 1995/96, the independently funded Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy says
** The government of western Maharashtra state, of which Bombay is the capital, sets target to create 4,000 megawatt hydroelectric power generation capacity by 2000-01, the Financial Express reports
** The Indian rupee opened steady at 35.72/73 per dollar. Dollar demand seen continuing with Monday's range expected at 35.67/71
MARKETS:
** Indian blue-chip shares drifted lower on Tuesday, dragged down by scandal-hit ITC stock which fell 18.50 rupees, or six percent, to 268.50
** The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange index fell 29.88 points, or 0.97 percent, to 3,062.84 after rising to 3,104.03
** The 50-share National Stock Exchange index lost 8.56 points to 881.57
** The Delhi share index dropped 9.74 points to 692.25
** The Calcutta index shed 5.09 points to 412.45
** The Madras index fell 4.56 points to 3,111.45
** The HSBC James Capel GDR Index closed down 0.83 points, or 1.35 percent, at 60.10 with the premium over the local market at 12.58 percent compared with Monday's 12.80 percent
STOCKS TO WATCH:

** Indian financial institutions, led by Industrial Development Bank of India and B.A.T Industries Plc, major shareholders of ITC Ltd, said on Tuesday they would review operations of the tobacco conglomerate at a board meeting on November 15
The share of scandal-hit ITC whose senior officials have
been arrested for alleged violation of foreign exchange rules, fell 18.50 rupees, or six percent, to 268.50 on Tuesday
** EIH Ltd, formally called East India Hotels, scheduled to unveil its first half results
** Paribas Capital Markets says it was upgrading shares of India's leading truck maker Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company to "buy" from "no action"
